plain: A tax or duty, especially on imported goods

webster.text: Any tax or tribute imposed by authority; particularly, a duty or tax laid by government on goods imported, and paid or secured by the importer at the time of importation.

example.quote: But if we surrender the impost, we shall still, by this new constitution, be held to pay our full proportion of the remaining debt, as if nothing had been done.
example.cite: Letters of Agrippa I-XI, Massachusetts Gazette, Nov. 1787-Jan. 1788
